item.title: Speed of Nepal’s Flash Floods Likely Overwhelmed Warning System, Experts Say
item.description: Scientists and disaster response researchers said Nepal’s early flood warning system relied on a conventional network of river gauges in this remote region.
item.dc:creator: Leo Sands and Binod Ghimire
item.media:description: Damage following flash floods in Trishuli, Nepal.

item.title: Is Haiti Safe for Haitian Deportees?
item.description: Stephen Miller said that Haiti is safe for Haitian deportees. Our White House correspondent Zolan Kanno-Youngs analyzed federal reports that say otherwise.
item.dc:creator: Zolan Kanno-Youngs, Gilad Thaler, Jon Miller, Ray Whitehouse and Stephanie Swart

item.title: ICE agent Christian Castro Released From Texas Jail After Minnesota Loses Court Fight
item.description: The state had sought to have the agent extradited from Texas to answer charges in Minneapolis related to an on-duty shooting that wounded an immigrant.
item.dc:creator: Mitch Smith and Ernesto Londoño
item.media:description: Christian Castro was one of thousands of agents sent to Minnesota in the winter as part of the Trump administration’s deportation campaign.

item.title: Backing Off French Issue Could Restart U.S. Trade Talks, Canadian Official Says
item.description: The minister in charge of trade with the United States was responding to comments by Jamieson Greer, the U.S. trade representative, to a Canadian broadcaster.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:description: Dominic LeBlanc, Canada’s minister responsible for trade with the United States, center, with Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada.

item.title: As Anger Grows Over Trump Tariffs, Some in Canada Want Out of U.S. F-35 Deal
item.description: A year into a government review of the purchase of as many as 88 F-35s, one premier says buying American warplanes makes no sense in the face of President Trump’s latest tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:description: The F-35 Lightning, made by American defense contractor Lockheed-Martin, costs between $82.5 million and $109 million per plane, depending on the variant.

item.title: How SSENSE, a Canadian Retailer, Is Grappling With Trump’s Tariffs
item.description: Ssense’s comeback efforts include moving a core part of its business to the United States so American customers can avoid hefty tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Peter Eavis
item.media:credit: Nasuna Stuart-Ulin for The New York Times
item.media:description: A stylist prepared a rack of clothes at a Ssense store in Montreal. The company, an online clothes retailer, is trying to lessen the burden of U.S. tariffs on its business.

item.title: Meta Projected It Could Spend $10 Billion on Anthropic’s A.I.
item.description: The social networking giant projected it could spend $10 billion annually on Anthropic’s tools, illustrating the friend-foe relationships underlying the A.I. race.

item.title: Trump’s Strength in Primaries is Clear. The Midterms Pose a Different Test.
item.description: The president’s pull with the party base has been clear and his resources are vast. But his low approval ratings make him a liability with swing voters.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk, Shane Goldmacher and Maggie Haberman
item.media:credit: Bryan Anselm for The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump campaigning with Representative Mike Lawler of New York in May. Republicans have to weigh Mr. Trump’s approval ratings against his popularity among his base.

item.title: Trump Raises Money in Texas With Control of the Senate in the Balance
item.description: Many Republicans are hoping for financial support from President Trump, whose fund-raising power in the party remains unmatched despite his low poll numbers.
item.dc:creator: Luke Broadwater
item.media:credit: Meridith Kohut for The New York Times
item.media:description: A cutout of President Trump in Cypress, Texas, during the Republican primary run-off for Senate between Attorney General Ken Paxton and Senator John Cornyn in May.

item.title: Democratic Socialists Are the Toast of the Party in Uruguay

item.description: At a festival on a disc golf course, on a peninsula in Iceland, waiting for the sky to descend into darkness.

item.title: Ratko Mladic, Murderous ‘Butcher of Bosnia,’ Dies at 83
item.description: A general during the Balkan wars of the 1990s, he was convicted in the killing of some 8,000 Muslims at Srebrenica, Europe’s deadliest massacre since World War II.
item.dc:creator: Dan Bilefsky
item.category: International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia
War Crimes, Genocide and Crimes Against Humanity
item.media:description: Ratko Mladic in Sarajevo in 1994. He was captured in 2011 and put on trial for genocide and war crimes.

item.title: Jury Begins Deliberations in Lindsay Clancy Murder Trial

item.dc:creator: Jacey Fortin and Maia Spoto

item.title: Roy Cohn, Robert Mapplethorpe and a Trump-Era Dilemma Over Free Speech
item.description: When a respected biographer tried to use a Mapplethorpe photograph of Roy Cohn for a book cover, worries about the wrath of Mr. Cohn’s protégé, President Trump, intervened.

item.title: DeSantis Administration Misspent $10 Million, Grand Jury Says
item.description: A charity tied to Gov. Ron DeSantis’s wife received the money from a state Medicaid settlement and diverted it to political committees supporting a cause favored by the governor.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei and David Ovalle
item.media:description: Casey DeSantis, Florida’s first lady, started the Hope Florida charity in 2021 and made it central to her public persona.

item.title: “Anxious Generation” Author Jonathan Haidt on the Meta Settlement
item.description: In “The Anxious Generation,” he laid out the evils of social media for kids. The landmark Meta settlement seems to agree.
item.dc:creator: Emma Goldberg
item.media:credit: Lila Barth for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jonathan Haidt’s 2024 book on the harms to children from social media was a best seller.

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg Wants to Make Sure YouTube and TikTok Share His Pain
item.description: Meta, the social media giant, agreed to change the way children interact with its apps. That could be trouble if its competitors don’t abide by the same rules.
item.dc:creator: Mike Isaac
item.media:description: To settle the suits, Meta agreed to drastically rein in children’s’ access to marquee products like Instagram and Facebook.

item.title: Administration Lawyer Chosen to Lead Panel Considering Trump Construction Projects
